Set control parameters for certified MCML estimation

Source: R/parameter_estimation.R
set_control_mcml.Rd

Non-Gaussian models are fitted by Monte Carlo maximum likelihood with importance sampling. The estimated log-likelihood is maximised on a fitting sample of draws, the estimate is corrected by one Newton step with the score from an independent validation sample, followed by further steps on that sample when the fitting sample predicts that one step leaves a residual, and the corrected estimate is certified with a second, fresh validation sample. The radius of the certificate, its allowance for the Monte Carlo error of that sample's score, is the larger of the radii of that sample and of a replicate of the same size drawn at the same estimate. The radius of one sample is estimated from its own draws, and is too small when the sample misses the rare draws of very large weight that dominate its error, which the replicate misses independently. The certificate is an approximate 95% bound, in statistical standard errors, on the Monte Carlo error of the estimate, that is its distance from the maximum of the exact likelihood that the fit has located. It is not an exact finite-sample guarantee, and it says nothing about whether that maximum is the highest (see check_maxima). If the certificate exceeds tolerance, the samples are enlarged to the size predicted to meet it and the fit is repeated.

Usage

set_control_mcml(
  initial_samples = 1000L,
  validation_samples = 5000L,
  max_samples = 16000L,
  max_stages = 4L,
  tolerance = 0.1,
  proposal = c("global", "laplace"),
  defensive_weight = 0.05,
  laplace_start = NULL,
  integrate_noise = "auto",
  check_maxima = TRUE,
  pc_prior = FALSE,
  pc_sigma_threshold = 1,
  pc_sigma_probability = 0.05,
  pc_scale_threshold = NULL,
  pc_scale_probability = 0.05
)

Arguments

initial_samples

Positive integer giving the number of draws in the fitting sample at the first stage. Defaults to 1,000.

validation_samples

Positive integer giving the number of draws in each validation sample, and in the replicate of the second, at the first stage. Later stages enlarge the validation samples in the same proportion as the fitting sample. Defaults to 5,000.

max_samples

Positive integer giving the largest permitted fitting sample. Defaults to 16,000.

max_stages

Positive integer giving the maximum number of stages. Defaults to 4.

tolerance

Positive number giving the largest accepted certificate, in statistical standard errors. Defaults to 0.1.

proposal

The importance distribution for the latent effects. "global" (the default) fits a Gaussian approximation to the whole conditional distribution of the latent effects, which keeps far more of the draws effective in sparse data than the Laplace approximation; "laplace" uses the Laplace approximation at the conditional mode. If the global approximation cannot be built at some parameter value, the stage is repeated with the Laplace approximation.

defensive_weight

Number in [0, 1) giving the share of importance draws taken from the prior distribution of the latent effects instead of the Gaussian approximation. This defensive mixture keeps the variance of the importance weights finite, which a Gaussian proposal alone does not in most spatial datasets, so that Monte Carlo errors are valid. Defaults to 0.05. Set to 0 to use the Gaussian approximation alone.

laplace_start

Logical or NULL. If TRUE, the Laplace approximation to the likelihood is first maximised from the starting values, and Monte Carlo maximum likelihood starts from that estimate. If the global importance distribution cannot be built at that estimate, as can happen in sparse data when it has a very large nugget, the fit starts from the starting values instead. NULL (the default) means TRUE, except where integrate_noise = TRUE integrates a term out, where it means FALSE, because there the Laplace approximation's spurious maximum moves to the spatial effect and the start from it costs more without certifying more fits. With integrate_noise = "auto" and a nugget as the only term that can be integrated out, the Laplace estimate chooses the form of the first stage, which with the nugget integrated out starts from the starting values.

integrate_noise

Logical, or "auto". If TRUE, a binomial or Poisson model integrates its independent Gaussian terms out of the likelihood numerically wherever the data allow it, and Monte Carlo maximum likelihood samples the spatial effect and the terms that stay. The model, its parameters and its likelihood are the same, so the option changes only how the same maximum is found. Sparse surveys with a large nugget, or with household effects, then keep far more effective draws. The terms are the nugget, whose levels are the locations, and each re() term. Records at a location with the same covariates, offset and random-effect levels are first combined into one unit. Then four rules apply.

  • A level of an re() term that holds a single unit, such as a household with one record or with records that do not differ, is integrated out of that unit's likelihood, and so is the nugget of a location with a single unit.

  • At a location with several units the nugget is integrated out as well, through an integral over the nugget of the units' own integrals, when the units share their covariates and offset and differ only in the levels of re() terms that each hold a single unit, as households of a village with covariates measured at the village do.

  • At a location with several units whose covariates or offsets differ, the units are integrated out in groups when every term but one has a single level shared by all of them and the levels of that one lie within the location. Its levels are the groups, such as the households of a cluster whose children differ in sex or birth order, each integrated over its own effect with its units' own covariates, and the nugget is integrated over the groups' integrals. Where every term is shared, the location is one group under its nugget.

  • At any other location the nugget stays sampled.

Every other level stays sampled. That includes the levels of an re() term that span several locations, such as villages or districts with several sampled points, and the levels at a location where two re() terms vary, such as households and the individuals within them. A term can be integrated out at some of its levels and sampled at others. check_fit() reports, for each term, at how many levels it was integrated out and at how many it stayed sampled. It works with any link, including a custom invlink. Where the nugget variance is close to zero the likelihood is nearly flat along it, and there the Monte Carlo estimate of its effect is noisier with the nugget integrated out than sampled, so fewer such fits are certified. With "auto" each stage of the fit integrates out the nugget if its variance at the start of the stage is at least 0.1 and samples it otherwise. The first stage takes the variance from the Laplace estimate, or from the starting values if laplace_start = FALSE. Every validation bank is then drawn with the nugget sampled and integrated out, and the two estimates of the score are combined with weights inverse to their Monte Carlo covariances, so the certificate rests on the more precise form, or on both. A bank whose importance weights have a heavy tail, with a Pareto k above 0.8, can understate its covariance and is left out of the combination. A model with an re() term that can be integrated out is fitted with "auto" as with TRUE, its re() terms and its nugget integrated out at every stage wherever the rules above allow. On simulated surveys of households that certified every fit, and in a fraction of the time of sampling, also where the nugget variance was zero, where switching the nugget alone sometimes failed. Defaults to "auto", which on simulated surveys with a nugget certified more fits than either form alone. A model without a nugget or re() terms is fitted in the same way whatever the value.

check_maxima

Logical. The certificate establishes Monte Carlo precision at the maximum found, not that no higher maximum exists. In sparse surveys an optimiser can stop at a maximum with a spatial scale far below the spacing between locations while a higher one exists at a longer scale, or the reverse. If TRUE (the default), a fitted scale below half the median distance between neighbouring locations is refitted from four dispersed starting values on the same Monte Carlo draws. After a fit at a longer scale the likelihood is evaluated at four shorter scales, with the coefficients and variance of the model with independent location effects (the limit of the model as the scale goes to zero, computed exactly by quadrature), and the fit is repeated from the best of them if it comes within 0.25 log-likelihood units of the fit. Exact lower bounds on the likelihood at short scales force a further search if they exceed the fitted log-likelihood. Separate maxima are compared on independent draws and the highest is kept, with a warning if it differs. A fit whose spatial correlation is numerically negligible is reported as numerically independent, with the scale unresolved and without standard errors or certificate. The screen of short scales and the exact bounds are available for the canonical links and models without unstructured random effects.

pc_prior

Logical. If TRUE, the spatial variance and scale are penalised by penalised-complexity priors (Fuglstad et al., 2019) and the estimate maximises the penalised likelihood on the log scale of the covariance parameters. This shrinks estimates away from degenerate solutions in small or sparse datasets. It is recommended for small or low-prevalence surveys, especially before prediction with parameter_uncertainty = TRUE in predict.RiskMap(). When the spatial variance is large and well identified, the penalty shrinks it somewhat towards zero, so the default is FALSE.

pc_sigma_threshold, pc_sigma_probability

The penalty sets P(sigma > pc_sigma_threshold) = pc_sigma_probability, where sigma is the spatial standard deviation on the scale of the linear predictor. Default 1 and 0.05.

pc_scale_threshold, pc_scale_probability

The penalty sets P(phi < pc_scale_threshold) = pc_scale_probability, where phi is the spatial scale in the units of the coordinates. By default the threshold is the median distance between neighbouring locations and the probability is 0.05.

Value

A control object of class RiskMap_control_mcml.

See also

glgpm(), set_control_mcmc()

Examples

control_mcml <- set_control_mcml(max_samples = 8000)
